name: Neuroscience Graduate Program (PhD)
summary: Interdisciplinary doctoral training in experimental and theoretical neuroscience, with three first-year lab rotations.

applicationFee.note: $120 for U.S. citizens/permanent residents; $140 international. International applicants are not eligible for central fee waivers. Request eligible waivers at least two weeks before the deadline.

english.toefl: 5.0 for tests on or after January 21, 2026; 80 for earlier tests
english.note: TOEFL/IELTS exemptions may apply for qualifying English-language education. Tests must be valid on the application deadline; electronic results only. Duolingo, TOEFL Home Edition and MyBest scores are not accepted.

requirements.note: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent and normally at least a 3.0 GPA are required. Only one UCSF graduate program application per cycle. Unofficial transcripts may be used for review; final official transcripts are due after admission. Foreign transcripts require an approved credential evaluation; check program-specific timing. Prerequisite guidance includes biology, physics, inorganic and organic chemistry, and calculus; not all admitted applicants have completed every prerequisite. Interfolio recommendations are not accepted.

international.note: Central policy currently says UCSF cannot process applications from people located in Iran or ordinarily resident in Iran; see official international admissions policy.

funding.note: All admitted students receive a stipend plus tuition and fees, subject to maintaining good standing. Includes medical, dental, vision and mental-health insurance, regardless of citizenship.
